title: Brant-X: A Unified Physiological Signal Alignment Framework

problem.claim: Existing physiological-signal research often focuses on a single signal type, overlooking correlations between EEG and other physiological signals that could improve performance across application scenarios.

gap.claim: Progress is constrained by scarce simultaneously collected physiological data, differing correlations among signals, and task-dependent correlation differences.

contributions.claim: Brant-X is a unified physiological signal alignment framework that models correlations between EEG and other physiological signals.
The framework uses an EEG foundation model to transfer EEG knowledge to other physiological signals in a data-efficient manner.
The framework introduces two-level alignment to align EEG and other physiological signals across different semantic scales.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance against task-agnostic and task-specific baselines across downstream tasks including sleep stage classification, emotion recognition, freezing of gait detection, and eye movement communication.
The authors report that arrhythmia-detection analysis and a case-study visualization further illustrate the effectiveness of knowledge transfer from EEG to other physiological signals.

narrative_sequence.summary: Physiological signals are useful for understanding human physiological states, but prior work commonly studies one signal type at a time.
EEG is correlated with other physiological signals, and exploiting these correlations may improve performance across scenarios.
The intended cross-signal modeling is hindered by limited simultaneous data and variation in signal and task correlations.
Brant-X transfers knowledge from an EEG foundation model and performs two-level semantic alignment across physiological signals.
The authors report strong downstream results across diverse tasks and supporting arrhythmia analysis and visualization.

source_observation.claim: The framework transfers knowledge from an EEG foundation model to other physiological signals and aligns signals at two semantic scales.

interpretation.claim: A strong representation learned from one richly studied modality may help address data scarcity in related modalities when cross-modal relationships are modeled explicitly.

application.claim: For multimodal physiological-signal systems, consider combining foundation-model transfer with alignment objectives that operate at multiple semantic levels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers to modalities, datasets, or tasks beyond those evaluated by the authors.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, sample sizes, evaluation metrics, or quantitative performance improvements.
The abstract does not describe the architecture or training procedure for the two-level alignment.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported state-of-the-art results.
